{{Short description|Local ring in mathematics}}
In [[algebra]], a '''generalized Cohen–Macaulay ring''' is a commutative Noetherian [[local ring]] <math>(A, \mathfrak{m})</math> of [[Krull dimension]] ''d'' > 0 that satisfies any of the following equivalent conditions:<ref>{{harvnb|Herrmann|Orbanz|Ikeda|1988|loc=Theorem 37.4.}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Herrmann|Orbanz|Ikeda|1988|loc=Theorem 37.10.}}</ref>
*For each integer <math>i = 0, \dots, d - 1</math>, the length of the ''i''-th [[local cohomology]] of ''A'' is finite:
*:<math>\operatorname{length}_A(\operatorname{H}^i_{\mathfrak{m}}(A)) < \infty</math>.
*<math>\sup_Q (\operatorname{length}_A(A/Q) - e(Q)) < \infty</math> where the sup is over all [[parameter ideal]]s <math>Q</math> and <math>e(Q)</math> is the [[multiplicity of a module|multiplicity]] of <math>Q</math>.
*There is an <math>\mathfrak{m}</math>-[[primary ideal]] <math>Q</math> such that for each system of parameters <math>x_1, \dots, x_d</math> in <math>Q</math>, <math>(x_1, \dots, x_{d-1}) : x_d = (x_1, \dots, x_{d-1}) : Q.</math>
*For each prime ideal <math>\mathfrak{p}</math> of <math>\widehat{A}</math> that is not <math>\mathfrak{m} \widehat{A}</math>, <math>\dim \widehat{A}_{\mathfrak{p}} + \dim \widehat{A}/\mathfrak{p} = d</math> and <math>\widehat{A}_{\mathfrak{p}}</math> is [[Cohen–Macaulay ring|Cohen–Macaulay]].

The last condition implies that the localization <math>A_\mathfrak{p}</math> is Cohen–Macaulay for each prime ideal <math>\mathfrak{p} \ne \mathfrak{m}</math>.

A standard example is the local ring at the vertex of an affine cone over a smooth [[projective variety]]. Historically, the notion grew up out of the study of a [[Buchsbaum ring]], a Noetherian local ring ''A'' in which <math>\operatorname{length}_A(A/Q) - e(Q)</math> is constant for <math>\mathfrak{m}</math>-primary ideals <math>Q</math>; see the introduction of.<ref>{{harvnb|Trung|1986}}</ref>
